original_value: Effective feature representations which should not only express the images individual properties, but also reflect the interaction among group images are essentially crucial for robust co-saliency detection. This paper proposes a novel deep learning co-saliency detection approach which simultaneously learns single image properties and robust group feature in a recurrent manner. Specifically, our network first extracts the semantic features of each image. Then, a specially designed Recurrent Co-Attention Unit (RCAU) will explore all images in the group recurrently to generate the final group representation using the co-attention between images, and meanwhile suppresses noisy information. The group feature which contains complementary synergetic information is later merged with the single image features which express the unique properties to infer robust co-saliency. We also propose a novel co-perceptual loss to make full use of interactive relationships of whole images in the training group as the supervision in our end-to-end training process. Extensive experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our approach in comparison with the state-of-the-art methods.

result.paraphrase: Robust co-saliency detection depends on effective feature representations that not only capture each image’s individual properties but also reflect interactions among images in a group. This paper introduces a new deep-learning co-saliency detection method that recurrently learns single-image properties and robust group features at the same time. Specifically, the network first extracts semantic features from each image. It then uses a specially designed Recurrent Co-Attention Unit (RCAU) to recurrently examine all images in the group, forming the final group representation through co-attention between images while suppressing noisy information. The resulting group feature, which contains complementary synergetic information, is later fused with the single-image features that describe unique properties to infer robust co-saliency. We further propose a novel co-perceptual loss that fully exploits the interactive relationships of the whole images in the training group as supervision in our end-to-end training process. Extensive experimental results show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
